roomNarratives.summary: The grand hall feels colder than it should. Something happened here recently.
Books are out of place, as if someone searched in haste.
The desk has been disturbed. Ashes in the grate still smell of burnt paper.
A secret chamber behind the study shelves — the Baron's private retreat.
Rain has darkened the gravel paths. The fountain murmurs in the silence.
A modest room for the household staff — neat, but plainly furnished.
Copper pots hang gleaming, but something feels wrong tonight.
The air is damp and close. Barrels and crates crowd the stone floor.
Rows of casks stretch into the gloom. Footsteps echo on the flagstones.

clueAssignments.hint: Baron Blackwood lies dead on the marble floor. Blood has pooled beneath his body, dark and still. Faint broom marks streak through the blood — someone tried to clean the scene.
The clock hands are frozen at eleven o'clock. The glass door is shattered — as if struck from inside.
Mrs. Clarke was finishing her rounds when she saw the Baron heading toward the library carrying several papers. He looked worried.
A torn appointment note lies among the books — the Baron was expected in the Study.
Ashes in the grate hold a charred ledger page — payments to Ytte that should not exist.
Blackwood's journal lies open on the desk, warning of smuggling and a missing silver key.
Something glints at the bottom of the fountain basin — a small silver key.
Inside the cabinet: forged manifests and ledgers in Ytte's hand.
A bloody apron hangs over the back of a chair.
A blood-stained crate sits crooked on the floor. Drag marks lead toward the wine cellar.
Behind the rearmost barrel — a carving knife, flecked with blood.

npcDialogOverrides.default: The scene is secured, Detective. Examine everything before you question anyone.

conditions.dialog: You have the evidence. Confront the killer, then report to me.
It appears Mrs. Clarke's statement checks out.
Mrs. Clarke was making her nightly rounds around eleven o'clock. Her room is upstairs — I'd start there.

npcDialogOverrides.default: My husband... I cannot bear to look at him. Please — find who did this.

conditions.dialog: Poor Mrs. Clarke... I should never have doubted her.
Mrs. Clarke was on her rounds at eleven. Those broom marks near his body... her room is upstairs. I hate to think it.

npcDialogOverrides.default: I was finishing my rounds when I saw the Baron heading toward the library carrying several papers. He looked worried.
npcDialogOverrides.blockedDialog: Mrs. Clarke keeps her eyes down. She won't say much until you've examined the scene downstairs.

npcDialogOverrides.default: The roast was perfect. I was in the kitchen all evening — ask anyone.

conditions.dialog: You cannot prove I— Stay back! I won't go quietly!
The cellars? I haven't been down there in weeks! You're chasing ghosts, Detective — leave me alone!
That apron isn't mine! Someone planted it — you have to believe me!
Those papers... Forged, every one! My handwriting? Anyone could copy that — I was framed!
A key from the fountain? I don't know anything about that. Why are you still questioning me?
Smuggling? In this house? I — I don't know what you're talking about. The Baron's journal lies.
Payments to me? Absurd. Whoever wrote that ledger page doesn't know the first thing about running a kitchen.
The Baron had papers with him? I saw nothing. I was at my station all evening — the roast wouldn't watch itself.
She's a good girl. I cannot believe anyone suspected her.
The maid was doing her rounds at eleven. They say there are broom marks by the body. Her room is on the east landing, upstairs.

npcDialogOverrides.default: Good evening, Detective. I trust you will be discreet.

conditions.dialog: The Baron did go to the Study after the Library. I showed him in myself.
Mrs. Clarke is a diligent woman. I am relieved her name is cleared.

npcDialogOverrides.default: I keep to the grounds. Heard shouting from the house, but I saw nothing.

conditions.dialog: Saw Ytte slip down toward the cellars late last night, apron bundled under his arm.
